title: Kufr, shirk and nifaq
intro: Disbelief, associating partners with Allah, and hypocrisy – what they are and how a Muslim stays away from them.

learn.text: O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book that He sent down upon His Messenger and the Scripture which He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly gone far astray.

learn.html: Kufr is not believing in Allah (SWT) and the other basic truths of the religion. It is one of the heaviest sins a person can commit. A person who commits kufr is called a kafir – a disbeliever. Kufr includes:

items: not believing in Allah and the other basic truths: His angels, His Books, His messengers, the Last Day and Allah’s decree,
insulting or mocking Allah or other holy things of Islam: the Qur’an, the Ka‘bah, the mosque, salah, fasting…
denying Allah’s duties (fard): salah, fasting, zakah, Hajj…
denying what Allah forbade (haram): alcohol, gambling, stealing, lying…
deliberately lying about Allah and His Messenger Muhammad (SAW).

learn.text: Say, "O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship. Nor are you worshippers of what I worship. Nor will I be a worshipper of what you worship. Nor will you be worshippers of what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion."

learn.html: Shirk is one of the heaviest sins: giving Allah (SWT) partners, believing that there are other gods besides Him. A person who commits shirk is called a mushrik. The Qur’an says that Allah will not forgive this sin unless the person repents:

learn.text: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.

learn.title: Major shirk (ash-shirk al-akbar)
learn.html: Worshipping someone besides Allah, or doing any act of worship for someone besides Him. The Arab mushriks believed in Allah, but they also believed in idols, thinking the idols brought them closer to Allah, or could help or harm them. The Qur’an called exactly that belief shirk.

learn.title: Minor shirk (ar-riya’)
learn.html: Showing off, or not being sincere in our deeds: doing good deeds to impress someone or to get something in this world, and not for Allah’s pleasure. Swearing by someone other than Allah, and wearing an amulet believing it can keep trouble away, are also minor shirk.

The Prophet (SAW) said: “What I fear most for you is minor shirk.” The companions asked: “What is minor shirk, O Messenger of Allah?” He said: “Showing off (riya’). On the Day of Judgement, when Allah rewards His servants, He will say to the show-offs: ‘Go to those you were showing off to in the world, and see if they will reward you.’” (Ahmad)
A person who has committed kufr or shirk must take a ghusl (full bath), repent for the sin and say the Shahadah.

learn.alt: One man shown with two faces, one in daylight and one at night
learn.caption: Hypocrites hide disbelief in their hearts, but in front of people they pretend to be believers.

learn.html: Nifaq is hiding disbelief in the heart while showing belief in words or actions in front of other people. A person who commits this sin is called a munafiq – a hypocrite. There are two kinds: minor nifaq (an-nifaq al-asghar) and major nifaq (an-nifaq al-akbar).

learn.text: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire - and never will you find for them a helper -

learn.html: At the beginning of Surah Al-Baqarah, Allah (SWT) speaks about the believers in only three ayat, about the disbelievers in two – and about the hypocrites in thirteen.

learn.text: And of the people are some who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers. They [think to] deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive not except themselves and perceive [it] not.

learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) described the hypocrite: “Whoever has these four qualities is a munafiq, and whoever has one of them has one quality of a munafiq until he leaves it: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; when he is trusted, he betrays; and when he argues, he goes beyond all limits.” (Bukhari)

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Whoever notices one of these qualities in themselves should repent and try to change their behaviour for the better as soon as possible.

Why was Surah Al-Kafirun revealed? A group of the Quraysh came to Muhammad (SAW) and said: “Follow our religion and we will follow yours. We will worship your God for a year, and then you worship our gods for a year.” The Prophet (SAW) said: “May Allah protect me from giving Him any partner.” Then Allah revealed this surah. The next morning the Prophet (SAW) went to the Ka‘bah, where the Quraysh were gathered, and recited Surah Al-Kafirun to the last ayah – and they lost all hope.

items.text: Not believing in Allah and His angels
Denying that salah is a duty
Doing good deeds only to show off
Hiding disbelief while pretending to be a believer

practice.title: Match the person and the sin

options: Giving Allah partners – believing in other gods besides Him

questions.q: What are the two kinds of shirk?
What must a person do who has committed kufr or shirk?
options: Take a ghusl, repent and say the Shahadah

questions.q: Which is one of the four qualities of a munafiq?
options: When he promises, he breaks it

questions.q: Where will the hypocrites be in the Hereafter?
options: In the lowest depths of the Fire

practice.title: Choose a task
prompts: ✏️ Find and write down the ayat at the start of Surah Al-Baqarah that speak about the munafiqun.
✏️ Make a poster of actions and qualities that belong to kufr – the behaviour of disbelievers.
